evidence: Campaign health plan pledges to protect Medicaid funding and enroll all eligible Coloradans; no provider-rate pledge (2026 campaign).
Pledges to lower drug costs and stop drug price collusion; related to but not the same as a drug-price board (2026 campaign).
Health plan pledges to build on the Colorado Option public plan to offer cheaper individual and family coverage (2026 campaign).
Pledges to protect families from medical debt collectors; no specific credit-report or cancellation plan (2026 campaign; KUNC Oct 2026).
Pledges to preserve Colorado's insulin price caps; says nothing on prior authorization (2026 campaign).
Wants large data centers to pay upfront deposits and direct infrastructure costs so they don't raise rates; called a data center bill his first priority (Oct 2026).
Blueprint says he will sign executive orders and push legislation to reform state housing efforts, targeting 40,000 attainable homes (plan updated May 2026).
Housing plan would expand down payment assistance for first-time buyers, including teachers and essential workers (2026 campaign).
Plan would protect renters, ban algorithmic rent collusion by corporate landlords and cut costs for 100,000 renters by 2035 (2026 campaign).
Vows to go after colluding corporate landlords and out-of-state investors, but proposes no limit on purchases (2026 campaign; KUNC Oct 2026).
Would speed up permitting and work with local governments to cut fees for homes under $600,000; no zoning preemption pledge (2026 campaign).
Pledges to support and expand Colorado's Universal Preschool program (2026 campaign).
Would integrate child care funding to make care more affordable and create a Childcare Solutions Fund; not a universal guarantee (2026 campaign).
Education plan pledges livable teacher wages so teachers need not work multiple jobs (2026 campaign).
Pledges to stand against privatizing or profiting off public schools; does not mention vouchers by name (2026 campaign).
Would enforce state laws limiting police role in immigration enforcement and barring sale of state sites for ICE detention; related policy (2026 campaign).
Pledges to defend Amendment 79, which put abortion rights in Colorado's constitution, and state abortion-rights laws (2026 campaign).
Proposed a 'Connecticut Option' with no co-pays at high-value hospitals, aimed at state workers, retirees and small firms, not open to all buyers (Feb 2026).
Said Connecticut is making up for most federal ACA exchange subsidy cuts and asked to extend the backfill fund (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Said the state told new data centers to slow down unless they add their own generation; no full cost-recovery plan (Feb 2026).
Says utilities can no longer bill ratepayers for charitable, legal, ad and lobbying costs, which shareholders now pay (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Proposed sending families an energy rebate of about $400 (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Touted the $400 million middle-class income tax cut enacted under him (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Touted the expanded state earned income tax credit, now about $1,000 for many workers, as already in place (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Said the state eliminated income tax for most seniors under his tenure (Feb 2026 State of the State).
Budget makes another large deposit in the child care endowment, aiming for universal early childhood education (Feb 2026).
Child care endowment is pitched as a path to universal early childhood education; no explicit universal pre-K pledge (Feb 2026).
Said Connecticut is protecting schools and courthouses from ICE arrests; the speech does not mention judicial warrants (Feb 2026).
Signed HB 8002 easing parking mandates and requiring town housing growth plans (Nov 2025), after vetoing the broader HB 5002 (June 2025).
His state program with a nonprofit has erased medical debt for hundreds of thousands; announced 97,000 more residents in June 2026.
Signed emergency law suspending the state gas excise tax (Mar 2022), later extended.
Signed the law creating Connecticut's paid family and medical leave program (June 2019).
Touts raising the minimum wage from about $10 to nearly $17 an hour on his watch, under the $15 law he signed (Feb 2026).
Said the state is being tough on medical fraud and hunting for savings; no inspector general or audit overhaul proposed (Feb 2026).
Framed his budget as 'no to more taxes'; general anti-tax-hike stance, not specific to a millionaire's tax (Feb 2026).
Signed a cap on Delmarva's recovery of nonessential infrastructure spending plus required PSC audits of utilities (Aug 2026), after attacking Delmarva overcharging (Jan 2026).
Asked the PSC to stop approving Delmarva rate hikes (Jan 2026); a retail-rate ask, not a push for wholesale or PJM price caps.
Urged the PSC to stop approving rate increases and praised the state energy affordability fund; no formal freeze or credits proposed (Jan 2026).
Signed bills making data centers pay a higher rate class, cover grid costs, bring their own power and forgo state tax incentives (Aug 2026).
Pledged the most streamlined permitting in the country and zoning reform with nine local governments (Jan 2026 State of the State).
Proposed nearly $50 million for early childhood, aimed at waitlists and employer-backed child care; not universal care (Jan 2026).
Condemned the federal ACA subsidy cuts as unconscionable; did not propose state money to replace them (Jan 2026).
Backed the Florida law making AI firms pay the new energy costs their facilities create and vows data centers won't raise bills; no tax-break rollback (Nov 2026).
Backed Amendment 3, which expands the homestead property-tax exemption, saying property taxes have roughly doubled in seven years (Oct 2026).
Pledges to expand Medicaid, end Georgia Pathways and stabilize rural hospitals (2026 campaign issues page).
Would create a Georgia Rx Savings Board to tackle prescription drug costs (2026 campaign issues page).
Blamed rising premiums on the failure to extend federal ACA subsidies and vows to keep Georgians covered; no state backfill plan (Apr and Aug 2026).
Says Georgia must slow down and reassess data center growth to protect families' utility bills; not a cost-recovery plan (2026 campaign).
Backs suspending Georgia's gas tax to ease fuel costs (Apr 2026 debate); a specific 28-cent target was not verified.
Would establish a statewide affordable housing trust fund modeled on the one she created as Atlanta mayor (Aug 2026).
Would expand down payment and renter assistance (2026 campaign issues page).
Would crack down on corporate landlords renting out large numbers of single-family homes (Aug 2026).
Proposes a 'Georgia Housing Fast Track' to streamline permitting; no zoning or preemption plan (2026 campaign).
Campaign lists a property tax and insurance relief plan; opposes abolishing property taxes; details not published (Sept 2026).
Would guarantee and fully fund pre-K for every 4-year-old and require full-day kindergarten (Apr and Aug 2026).
Lists universal child care as a goal on her campaign issues page (2026).
Would raise average starting teacher pay from $48,000 to $60,000 and end state income tax for teachers (Aug-Sept 2026).
Vows to fight to restore abortion rights and repeal Georgia's six-week 'heartbeat' law (Apr 2026 debate; campaign site).
